{{short description|Type of graph labeling}}

In [[graph theory]], an '''edge-graceful labeling''' is a type of [[graph labeling]] for [[simple graph|simple]], [[connected graph]]s in which no two distinct [[edge (graph theory)|edge]]s connect the same two distinct [[Vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] and no edge connects a vertex to itself. 

Edge-graceful labelings were first introduced by Sheng-Ping Lo in his seminal paper.<ref name="lo">{{cite conference | zbl=0597.05054 |last=Lo | first=Sheng-Ping | title=On Edge-Graceful Labelings of Graphs | conference=Sundance Conference, Utah | book-title=Congressus Numerantium | volume=50 | year=1985 | pages=231–241 }}</ref>

== Definition ==

Given a graph {{mvar|G}}, we denote the set of its edges by {{math|''E''(''G'')}} and that of its vertices by {{math|''V''(''G'')}}. Let {{mvar|q}} be the [[cardinality]] of {{math|''E''(''G'')}} and {{mvar|p}} be that of {{math|''V''(''G'')}}. Once a labeling of the edges is given, a vertex of the graph is labeled by the sum of the labels of the edges incident to it, [[Modular arithmetic|modulo]] {{mvar|p}}. Or, in symbols, the induced labeling on a vertex is given by
:<math>V(u)=\Sigma E(e) \mod |V(G)|</math>
where {{math|''V''(''u'')}} is the resulting value for the vertex {{mvar|u}} and {{math|''E''(''e'')}} is the existing value of an edge {{mvar|e}} incident to {{mvar|u}}.

The problem is to find a labeling for the edges such that all the labels from {{math|1}} to {{mvar|q}} are used once and that the induced labels on the vertices run from {{math|0}} to {{math|''p'' − 1}}. In other words, the resulting set of labels for the edges should be {{math|{1, 2, …, ''q''<nowiki>}</nowiki>}}, each value being used once, and that for the vertices should be {{math|{0, 1, …, ''p'' − 1<nowiki>}</nowiki>}}.

A graph {{mvar|G}} is said to be edge-graceful if it admits an edge-graceful labeling.

== Examples ==
=== Cycles ===
[[File:Edge graceful c5.svg|150px|thumb|An edge-graceful labeling of {{math|''C''{{sub|5}}}}]]

Consider the [[cycle graph|cycle]] with three vertices, {{math|''C''{{sub|3}}}}. This is simply a triangle. One can label the edges 1, 2, and 3, and check directly that, along with the induced labeling on the vertices, this gives an edge-graceful labeling. Similar to paths, {{mvar|C{{sub|m}}}} is edge-graceful when {{mvar|m}} is odd and not when {{mvar|m}} is even.<ref>{{cite journal | author=Q. Kuan, S. Lee, J. Mitchem, and A. Wang | title=On Edge-Graceful Unicyclic Graphs | journal=Congressus Numerantium | volume=61 | year=1988 | pages=65–74 }}</ref>

=== Paths ===

Consider a [[path (graph theory)|path]] with two vertices, {{math|''P''{{sub|2}}}}. Here the only possibility is to label the only edge in the graph 1. The induced labeling on the two vertices are both 1. So {{math|''P''{{sub|2}}}} is not edge-graceful.

Appending an edge and a vertex to {{math|''P''{{sub|2}}}} gives {{math|''P''{{sub|3}}}}, the path with three vertices. Denote the vertices by {{math|''v''{{sub|1}}}}, {{math|''v''{{sub|2}}}}, and {{math|''v''{{sub|3}}}}. Label the two edges in the following way: the edge {{math|(''v''{{sub|1}}, ''v''{{sub|2}})}} is labeled 1 and {{math|(''v''{{sub|2}}, ''v''{{sub|3}})}} labeled 2. The induced labelings on {{math|''v''{{sub|1}}}}, {{math|''v''{{sub|2}}}}, and {{math|''v''{{sub|3}}}} are then 1, 0, and 2 respectively. This is an edge-graceful labeling and so {{math|''P''{{sub|3}}}} is edge-graceful.

Similarly, one can check that {{math|''P''{{sub|4}}}} is not edge-graceful.

In general, {{mvar|P{{sub|m}}}} is edge-graceful when {{mvar|m}} is odd and not edge-graceful when it is even. This follows from a necessary condition for edge-gracefulness.

== A necessary condition ==

Lo gave a necessary condition for a graph with {{mvar|q}} edges and {{mvar|p}} vertices to be edge-graceful:<ref name="lo"/>{{math|''q''(''q'' + 1)}} must be [[Modular arithmetic#Congruence|congruent]] to {{math|{{sfrac|''p''(''p'' − 1)|2}} mod ''p''}}. In symbols:
:<math>q(q+1) \equiv \frac{p(p-1)}{2} \mod p.</math>

This is referred to as '''Lo's condition''' in the literature.<ref>{{cite journal | author=L. Lee, S. Lee and G. Murty | title=On Edge-Graceful Labelings of Complete Graphs: Solutions of Lo's Conjecture | journal=Congressus Numerantium | volume=62 | year=1988 | pages=225–233 }}</ref> This follows from the fact that the sum of the labels of the vertices is twice the sum of the edges, modulo {{mvar|p}}. This is useful for disproving a graph is edge-graceful. For instance, one can apply this directly to the path and cycle examples given above.

== Further selected results ==

*The [[Petersen graph]] is not edge-graceful.
*The [[star graph]] <math>S_m</math> (a central node and ''m'' legs of length 1) is edge-graceful when ''m'' is [[even number|even]] and not when ''m'' is [[odd number|odd]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=D. Small| title=Regular (even) Spider Graphs are Edge-Graceful | journal=Congressus Numerantium | volume=74 | year=1990 | pages=247–254 }}</ref>
*The [[friendship graph]] <math>F_m</math> is edge-graceful when ''m'' is odd and not when it is even.
* [[Regular tree]]s, <math>T_{m,n}</math> (depth ''n'' with each non-leaf node emitting ''m'' new vertices) are edge-graceful when ''m'' is even for any value ''n'' but not edge-graceful whenever ''m'' is odd.<ref>{{cite journal | author=S. Cabaniss, R. Low, J. Mitchem| title=On Edge-Graceful Regular Graphs and Trees | journal= Ars Combinatoria | volume=34 | year=1992 | pages=129–142 }}</ref>
*The [[complete graph]] on ''n'' vertices, <math>K_n</math>, is edge-graceful unless ''n'' is [[singly even]], <math>n=2\mod 4</math>.
*The [[ladder graph]] is never edge-graceful.
